output.brief: The Kestria buffering is almost certainly not the CDN. Tessaline serves every client in Kestria, yet only the smart-TV app 5.2 is buffering (about 5.9% rebuffering versus 0.6–0.7% for the 5.1 devices with auto-update off, the web player, and the mobile apps). The pattern holds across all three ISPs, and the rise began on 9 October, the day app 5.2 went live everywhere. The likely cause is 5.2's adaptive-streaming behaviour, which also starts video faster, so it is probably being too aggressive on these devices. The handball launch does not explain it, since match nights were flat. Moving traffic back to Corvane, withholding fees and sending a breach notice would target the wrong party. Muting the alert would hide an ongoing problem. What to do next: roll back 5.2's adaptive settings for Kestria to the 5.1 behaviour and pause the wider 5.2 rollout. That is reversible and fits the evidence. Confidence is moderate: the breakdown came from an ad hoc query, and cancellations may reflect the price rise as well as buffering. Add app version and ISP to the dashboard, and confirm the fix by checking 5.2 rebuffering after rollback.
